analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation table row in docs/architecture/inference.md, line 2126 of both base and head. It describes how the `stop` parameter is scoped: Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans per request through `ReasoningStopScope`, and the native block engine (diffusion Gemma) matches the whole output with no scope. The supplied units are base_text excerpts at lines 2465-3234, which contain no changed lines. I examined them for context only and found them unchanged. The patch itself is documentation and alters no code, key handling, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, or cache policy.

I checked the new text against the threat model. The stop-string scoping behaviour concerns output truncation semantics, not the sealed coordinator-to-provider channel (TB-002/A-001), the prefix cache (T-041), or attestation (TB-009/TB-011). The row could only matter if the real implementation in EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift or ReasoningStopScope diverged from it. That source is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract and not as a finding. A possible security-relevant interaction is that a stop-sequence match inside a reasoning or tool-call span would leak or truncate content differently. The reported sequence is said to replay the request's scope, but this cannot be verified here. No threat-model update appears necessary. The unchanged text in the base excerpts is outside this PR's changes and I did not restate any pre-existing issue.
